extracted.intended_audience: German-speaking readers, students, historians, and practitioners interested in public relations, propaganda, and corporate/government communication
extracted.subtask_description: High-level principles for practicing or understanding public relations/propaganda as articulated in Edward Bernays' 1928 work, with emphasis on language, methods, audience influence, and examples. Useful for writers and communicators designing PR messaging or studying the foundations of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_clear_language
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in clear language and avoid contemporary industry jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "In klarer Sprache, frei vom heute verbreiteten Branchenvokabular, legt er ... dar" — Bernays presents ideas plainly rather than using specialized PR buzzwords; this favors accessibility and persuasive clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: distinguish_pr_from_advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly differentiate public relations from advertising in purpose and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "legt er ... dar, worin sich Public Relations von Werbung unterscheidet." Guidance: explain how PR works beyond paid advertising, focusing on shaping public opinion and social processes rather than transactional promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: justify_influence_of_mass_opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a rationale for why influencing mass opinion is necessary and legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "Er begründet, warum es von elementarer Bedeutung ist, die Meinung der Massen zu steuern" — the work argues for the importance of steering public opinion; effective PR should explicitly situate its aims within a rationale (e.g., enabling progress or social change).

rubrics_metrics.name: use_concrete_examples_to_explain_methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate techniques with concrete, real-world examples showing how influence is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "und erklärt einem ganz konkreten Beispielen, wie das geht." Guidance: demonstrative case studies or specific examples are required to show application of abstract PR principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: be_candid_about_psychological_tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and explain psychological techniques, including targeting unconscious drives, used to sell products or implement unpopular measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "Freimütig berichtet der Freud-Neffe, wie sich über den gezielten Zugriff auf das Unbewusste Waren verkaufen oder gesellschaftlich unpopuläre Maßnahmen durchsetzen lassen." Guidance: Bernays advocates frank discussion of psychological methods and their practical use in persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: rehabilitate_or_reframe_problematic_terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where terminology has negative connotations (e.g., 'propaganda'), consciously reframe or rename the practice to gain legitimacy (e.g., 'public relations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "Da der Begriff sich nicht so einfach rehabilitieren lässt, prägt er ... ein anderes Wort für die Tätigkeit: 'Public Relations'." Guidance: strategic renaming and framing are tools to change public perception of the practice itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: acclimatize_public_to_change_and_progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Design communications to habituate the public to change and progress so new ideas or measures become acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text (quote): "Propaganda gewöhnt die Öffentlichkeit den Wandel und den Fortschritt." Guidance: a key objective of persuasive campaigns is to normalize change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: design_for_corporate_and_government_communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop principles and tactics that apply to both corporate and government communication contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: "Er schafft damit bis heute gültige Grundlagen für Unternehmens- und Regierungskommunikation" — Bernays' methods are presented as foundational for both sectors; guidance: craft strategies that consider institutional aims and public governance implications.
